message.content: **Summary:** I researched Apple's latest results and news, then bought 44 shares of AAPL at a limit price of $223.00 (filled at $223.00, ~$9,812 total), which sits within the mandate's $10,000 per-order and $20,000 daily caps and is only ~0.1% above the $222.70 market quote at the time. The decision rested on Apple's fiscal 2024 10-K (filed 2024-11-01) showing revenue of $391,035 million, net income of $93,736 million, and diluted EPS of $6.08 — figures that include a one-time $10.2 billion tax charge — plus the Q4 release showing quarterly revenue of $94.9 billion, up 6% year over year, with services growing 13%. News flow was neutral-to-constructive: shares were roughly flat around $222 as investors weighed iPhone 16 demand against the gradual Apple Intelligence rollout, so I sized the position modestly rather than aggressively. No money was moved out of the account (cash was $50,000 with an existing 100-share MSFT position), and I placed only this one order, leaving $10,188 of today's $20,000 budget unused.
message.reasoning: Order filled at 223.00, 44 shares = $9,812. Within $10k per order and $20k total. Summarize.
